targets.authors: Rand DG, Greene JD, Nowak MA
targets.title: Spontaneous giving and calculated greed.
targets.evidence_quote:
In an attempt to replicate Rand and colleagues'
[1]
intuitive-cooperation effect, we conducted three experiments in which we sequentially changed the three abovementioned aspects of the procedure in our Experiment 1.
targets.outcome_quote: Hence, the outcomes of our experiments are inconsistent with Rand and colleagues' original finding.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly report failure of the intuitive-cooperation effect.

targets.authors: Rand DG, Peysakhovich A, Kraft-Todd GT, Newman GE, Wurzbacher O, et al.
targets.title: Social heuristics shape intuitive cooperation.
targets.evidence_quote:
Considering that Mechanical Turk workers from the United States are experienced, and that the intuitive-cooperation effect interacts with experience, it might be possible that Rand and colleagues
[8]
recent failures to find an intuitive-cooperation effect in Mechanical Turk experiments as well as our failures to find such an effect in Experiment 1 and in Experiments 2a, 2b and 2c are due to the Mechanical Turk population becoming increasingly experienced in playing public good games. In order to test this experience hypothesis of our replication failures, we conducted a third experiment.
targets.outcome_quote: In Experiment 3, we again failed to demonstrate an intuitive-cooperation effect. This replication failure contradicts the experience hypothesis because it was obtained using naïve participants only.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly report failure of the intuitive-cooperation effect.

reasoning: New samples test the published intuitive-cooperation effect and, in Experiment 3, the published experience moderator claim. The 2014 paper is a target specifically for the latter claim; other replications mentioned in the review are not targets.
